_meta.usage: a whole plate in either format, or just its three letters: ABC-1234 (grey or red, 1990–2020), ABC1D23 (Mercosul, 2018 on), ABC. Other shapes (the yellow AB-1234 plates of 1969–1990, Argentina's AB 123 CD) don't fit this table and are not looked up. Uruguay's plates are also ABC 1234 and DO match a state here: near the Uruguayan border, check for a URUGUAY band first
_meta.note: The three letters name the UF where the vehicle was FIRST registered: each Detran received letter blocks from Denatran/Senatran, and the Mercosul plate (2018 on) kept them, turning the second digit into a letter (ABC-1234 → ABC1C34). A vehicle keeps its letters for life: until each state adopted Mercosul plates (September 2018–February 2020) a move only swapped the grey plate's metal strip with UF and town; since then a move to another municipality or state requires a Mercosul plate, which shows no town or UF, so on a recent plate the letters are the only regional hint. Rental and fleet cars and trucks travel far from their registration state (most rental cars carry Minas Gerais registrations). Special combinations: RIO (Rio de Janeiro, first Mercosul plates, 2018), UAI (Minas Gerais), SAV (São Paulo's partial block, then Ceará). Keys are single combinations: 9833 backed by two lists or by Detran-PR; 3889 only in en.wikipedia's per-state table and 5 only in its alphabetical list (unverified, with a note); 16 that the two lists assign to different UFs (both listed, unverified); and SAV, split by number between São Paulo and Ceará (both rows unverified). The series lists are community compilations (en.wikipedia, updated 2025–2026; a 2014 snapshot at carrosnors.com.br); Senatran publishes no table.
_meta.miss_note: combination not in the table: a series newer than the table (it ends at UKQ), a block the source leaves unassigned (TQF–TQN, TVE–TVJ, TWL–TWX, UGW–UHI, UIJ–UIU), or a misread letter (O/Q/D, I/J)
